subject: Clarification needed: EU data-jurisdiction clause blocking DPA execution
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medfincloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@medfincloud.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — final steps for signature

Jonas —

Thanks for the latest DPA draft. Our procurement team ran the redlines and raised one major blocker: the clause about cross-border transfer mechanisms in section 4.2. Our legal team requires either a clear supplement that references SCCs (with confirmed subprocessors) or a contractual commitment to keep EU customer data in EU-backed infrastructure.

Two asks before we can sign:
- A statement from Redwood confirming the list of active subprocessors and whether any will process EU personal data outside the EU.
- Confirmation that key management controls (KMS) for EU customers can be scoped to EU regions (we need an HSM/KMS guarantee or an exception).

Procurement is standing by — they have the DocuSign envelope open but won't proceed until legal signs off. Can someone on your side confirm? The deal is timing-sensitive for our year-end migration.

Elena
Director, Procurement — MedFinCloud

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medfincloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — final steps for signature

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers and next steps:  
1) Subprocessors: I attached a current export of our subprocessor list and a redline (MedFin_DPA_redlines_v3.docx) that attempts to surface allowed transfer routes. Active subprocessors that will handle EU personal data are listed; only one (EdgeAccel LLC) has a potential cross-border processing footprint (EU->US) for telemetry aggregation.
2) KMS/HSM: We can offer region-scoped key material for EU customers using our partner KMS (we use customer-scoped keys for Dedicated/Private customers, but hosted customers can get EU-scoped KMS on request). I need to confirm the precise contractual language — looping in Laura from Legal to propose wording.

Laura — can you review the attached redline and propose an exception path or addendum language that will satisfy MedFin's request on SCCs/KMS? If we can provide a JIT (just-in-time) exception path for procuring EU-KMS for this account, that may unblock the DocuSign envelope.

Tom — tagging you for visibility on the procurement deadline (Elena mentioned year-end migration).

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference

Attachment: MedFin_DPA_redlines_v3.docx

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medfincloud.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — final steps for signature

Elena / team —

Thanks for the detail. I reviewed MedFin_DPA_redlines_v3.docx and have two notes:  
1) SCCs: We can incorporate standard EU SCCs as an addendum; however, we cannot unilaterally promise to keep all EU customer data solely in EU regions for hosted customers without a Dedicated/Private contract amendment. The reason: our telemetry and metrics pipelines aggregate anonymized signals in the US for product analytics. We can agree to exclude personal data from that pipeline or pseudonymize it — but that requires a technical change and a short implementation window.
2) KMS commitment: For hosted customers we offer optional EU-region KMS encryption keys via our cloud partner. We can commit in contract to use EU-scoped KMS for MedFin's production customer data, conditional on a small one-time onboarding and noted fees.

Proposed contract language (high level) to add as an exhibit:
- Exhibit: EU Data Controls — Redwood will restrict processing of Customer Production Data to EU regions except for limited operations (describe telemetry/pseudonymization), and will use EU-region KMS for encryption at rest for Customer Production Data. Implementation details and any one-time onboarding fees will be recorded in a mutually-executed SOW.

If MedFin accepts the exhibit and the SOW model, Legal can sign within 48 hours. Alternatively, if they need an exception without switching to a Dedicated/Private plan, we need CISO-level approval on compensating controls (Neha / Vivek, please review).

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medfincloud.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@medfincloud.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — final steps for signature

Laura / Jonas —

Thanks for the options and the proposed exhibit. Procurement really needs the DocuSign envelope completed this week. A few clarifications from MedFin legal:
- The SOW approach is acceptable if the exhibit is contractually binding and the onboarding timeline is guaranteed (MedFin cannot leave a migration window open without controls).
- There is some sensitivity around the telemetry pipeline — MedFin's auditors treat aggregated telemetry differently depending on whether it is reversible. Can you confirm pseudonymization details in writing?

On the DocuSign side — our admin reports the envelope shows Redwood as the last signer, but they paused because procurement needs the KMS/region language to be explicit in the DPA. I can re-open if we have a firm exhibit. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/packets/0a1b2c3d-medfin-dpa (currently paused).

If you prefer, we can accept an interim risk acceptance letter from Redwood's CISO that commits to the exhibit roadmap and timeline while formal SOW is executed. That would let procurement complete DocuSign and avoid slipping the migration.

Elena

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-19T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — final steps for signature

Team —

I reviewed the exhibit language Laura proposed. High level: we can sign off on a binding exhibit that commits to EU-region KMS and pseudonymization of telemetry, but with these caveats:
- We must define "pseudonymization" in measurable terms (irreversible tokenization, no reversible mapping stored outside EU). Implementation requires a 2-week engineering change window and an ops verification run.
- For EdgeAccel LLC (subprocessor), we require a subprocessors attestation confirming they will not transfer identifiable EU personal data outside the EU; if they cannot, we must either remove that subprocessor from the account or apply additional encryption controls.

I'm willing to provide a CISO-level risk acceptance letter that commits to the timeline (2 weeks to implement pseudonymization and provide attestation from EdgeAccel), conditional on MedFin executing the DPA in DocuSign and agreeing to a short SOW to capture onboarding tasks and fees. The letter will include compensating controls (access logging, quarterly attestation reports, and an incident response SLA).

If Legal is happy with the exact exhibit wording, I can draft the risk acceptance letter by EOD tomorrow and sign it.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medfincloud.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Baxter <tbaxter@medfincloud.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20T17:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — final steps for signature

Elena / Tom — Laura / Vivek — quick summary and proposed ask for decision: 

Summary:
- Redwood can provide an Exhibit committing to EU-region KMS for MedFin production data and will implement telemetry pseudonymization within 2 weeks.
- Vivek will provide a CISO risk acceptance letter that covers compensating controls and a timeline; EdgeAccel attestation is required to finalize the exhibit.
- Legal will include the exhibit in the DPA; Procurement can then complete DocuSign.

Ask:
- Can MedFin agree to execute the DPA in DocuSign if Redwood provides the CISO risk acceptance letter and a signed SOW to follow within 5 business days? This is our recommended path to avoid stalling the migration. If you accept, we will:
  1) Upload the exhibit into the DPA today.
  2) Vivek will send the risk acceptance letter by EOD tomorrow.
  3) Laura will finalize the SOW and the onboarding fee estimate for signature.

If MedFin cannot accept this path, we understand and will prepare an alternate: pause migration windows and require a Dedicated/Private deployment contract (longer lead time). That will unfortunately push timelines past year-end.

Attachment: SOW-MedFin-2026.pdf

Jonas Weber
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
